model_system: single-layer kagome noncollinear antiferromagnet KFe3(OH)6(SO4)2 (potassium iron jarosite), using a spin-wave/Holstein-Primakoff bosonic Bogoliubov Hamiltonian with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction

key_params.formalism: large-S Holstein-Primakoff expansion in particle-hole (BdG) space
key_params.response_formula: intrinsic magnon spin Nernst conductivity from Kubo linear response with spin Berry curvature, Eq. (15)
key_params.temperature_drive: temperature gradient represented by pseudo-gravitational potential χ(r) with χ=-T(r)/T to linear order
key_params.lattice: 2D kagome antiferromagnet, 3 magnetic sites per unit cell
key_params.magnetic_order: noncollinear 120-degree antiferromagnetic order with small out-of-plane canting
key_params.interaction_of_interest: in-plane Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction generates the spin Nernst response
key_params.band_treatment: diagonalize σ3 H_k via paraunitary transformation T_k; use positive-energy magnon bands n<=N
key_params.observable: spin current j_O with O=S^alpha; source/torque terms discussed but focus placed on spin-current response
key_params.berry_curvature: generalized spin Berry curvature Ω^{Sγλ}_{n,k,β} entering J^γ_λ
key_params.statistics: Bose-Einstein distribution g(ε_nk) and c1(x)=(1+x)ln(1+x)-xln x

headline_claim: The paper predicts a measurable intrinsic magnon spin Nernst response in single-layer KFe3(OH)6(SO4)2 induced by in-plane Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction.
replication_difficulty: high - requires reconstructing the full noncollinear magnon BdG Hamiltonian, paraunitary diagonalization, and Brillouin-zone integration of spin Berry curvature; the excerpt gives no complete numerical parameter set.
